text:
B: Hiya! Darren, is it? I'm Lauren. Oh, you're the one with the Tigers throw!
A: That's me. Alright, Lauren.
B: You alright, duck? How've you found these? I've loved it, honestly, I've talked the ears off everyone.
A: Yeah, they've been alright, actually. Better than I thought. I nearly didn't bother.
B: Glad you did! Where are you, Yorkshire?
A: Castleford. You're Derby, aren't you? Bethany said. She said you were a laugh.
B: Aw, did she? She's lovely, isn't she. I had her second. I'm trying to get her to sell her pressed flowers.
A: She should. She's got a good eye, you can tell. She were in bits about that shop, mind.
B: I know. We bonded over being out of work, actually. I was a fitness instructor at the leisure centre, and the new company came in, cut the classes, and that was me. Signing on now, the glamour.
A: That's rough, that. Same story everywhere. Somebody in an office with a spreadsheet decides, and it's never them that loses out, is it.
B: Exactly! Not one of them had ever been to a class. What do you do?
A: Joiner. Housing association. Doors, kitchens, floors, all over Wakefield district. Me knees are shot.
B: Oh, me boyfriend's the same with his back, he drives a forklift at a warehouse near the airport. He comes home and lies on the floor groaning. Cat sits on him.
A: Ha. What cat have you got? I saw him in your photo. Big grey lad.
B: Biscuit! He's a rescue, he's massive. Do you have one?
A: Not mine. Next door's keeps coming in through the back door. I've started buying him food, so that's on me, really.
B: Aw, he's adopted you! That's how it starts. Then you're buying a little bed and everything.
A: Don't. I've already put a cushion out. Don't tell anyone.
B: Your secret's safe. So, Tigers. My dad'd get on with you, he's Rams mad. I go with him sometimes. He's not been well lately, though, so we've just been watching it at his.
A: Sorry to hear that. Hope he's alright.
B: Yeah, he's... we don't really know yet, they're doing tests. Anyway! Sorry, didn't mean to go there.
A: No, you're alright. I lost me dad when I were twenty-nine. You make the most of the matches, do you know what I mean. That's what I'd do.
B: Yeah. Yeah, I will. Thanks, Darren.
A: Anyway. Sorry. I'm a cheery one, me.
B: No, you're fine! Do you go away much? I'm always looking at holidays online, Thailand, Iceland, then I end up in a caravan in Skegness with me mum.
A: Filey for me. I keep saying I'll do Krakow. Mate went, said it were brilliant. I never book it. It's the airport, all that queuing and taking your belt off.
B: Oh, East Midlands is dead easy, you'd be fine! They do Krakow from there, I think. Cheap as anything.
A: Do they?
B: Pretty sure. You've got no excuse now, duck. I'm holding you to it.
A: Go on, then. I'll look tonight. After me pie.
B: Pie and a holiday, that's a good evening. I'm on a cheese cob, I'm so jealous of your—
